column2:
Does the national portal offer to its users a way to programmatically query the metadata via a SPARQL access point?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide the direct-URL to this feature.
column4: new question
column7:
The module enabled the Portal to interact with other web resources. https://data.gov.ua/sparql
https://data.gov.ua/pages/aboutuser2 
However, due to security risks and enemy cyber-attacks, the CKAN SPARQL Interface Extension module has been disabled, as the module's web form provided the ability to query other servers in order to download datasets published for public access using SPARQL search. Before full-scale invasion users had the opportunity to send a SPARQL query, view the search results and export them in RDF serializations (RDF/XML, Turtle) and in open machine-readable formats (CSV, JSON).
The new portal modernization includes the restoration of SPARQL search, but it will be limited to the Open Data portal only.
Results of the Portal's audit: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VWDAYpzZjJ9ofsWj2soXl5RGlWEG5y2K/view?usp=sharing, technical task: https://drive.google.com/file/d/15gZo1SvO3WKHWXOta7PwVQ8JZiPRSpR2/view?usp=sharing, technical and economic justification: https://drive.google.com/file/d/19U6kVfO4SU6bnG0_yWfIiY_xUGsBIINn/view?usp=sharing.

column2: 2.3 Data provision

To what degree do public sector data providers contribute data to the portal? 

For Explanation:
*Please describe what is the agreed approach.
* If less than the majority of data providers, please briefly explain why (e.g. technical incompatibilities, governance aspects, low awareness etc.).
column4: According to legislation, all public sector data providers have to publish their data on the portal. On the central level, approximately 100% of providers publish their data (at least 1 data set). On the regional/local level more than 80% of data providers publish their data(at least 1 data set) Portal team constantly monitors the level of data sets publication by both central and regional/local authorities. The main reasons why not all the required datasets are published are technical incompatibilities of publishers and lack of human resource

column2:
Were there concrete actions taken to assist these data providers with their publication process?

For Explanation:
* If yes, could you provide some examples of the actions taken in this regard.
column3: yes, or all public sector data providers already publish data
column4:
Instruction and other materials helping data providers with their publication process are published at the portal https://data.gov.ua/pages/835-rec-index 
Data providers can get technical support through the emails, chat or calls by the portal team.

Moreover, Ministry of Digital Transformation has launched a curriculum - "Intensive on Open Data for data providers - central executive bodies and local self-government bodies". The purpose of the intensives is to improve the quality of datasets of central executive bodies and local self-government bodies. To this end, the participants of the Intensive together with the experts:
diagnose their own Open Data policy;
analyze its strengths and weaknesses;
draw up an action plan to help effectively publicize datasets and begin implementing it.

These intensives are carried out monthly (separated for central executive bodies and local self-government bodies) and last for 2 weeks including both intramural and asynchronous forms of work. Representatives from central executive bodies and local self-government bodies have already successfully finished 14 intensives (2023 year). In 2022 the 37 intensives were conducted.

Instruction (https://bit.ly/3dq9MYZ) and other materials helping data providers with their publication process are published at the portal https://data.gov.ua/pages/835-rec-index Data providers can get technical support through the emails, chat or calls by the portal team. Also Ministry of Digital Transformation has launched a curriculum - "Intensive on Open Data for data providers - central executive bodies and local self-government bodies". The purpose of the intensives is to improve the quality of datasets of central executive bodies and local self-government bodies. To this end, the participants of the Intensive together with the experts: diagnose their own Open Data policy; analyze its strengths and weaknesses; draw up an action plan to help effectively publicize datasets and begin implementing it. These trainings are carried out monthly (separated for central executive bodies and local self-government bodies) and last for 2 weeks including both intramural and asynchronous forms of work. Moreover, from the end of 2023, the Open Data Academy is implemented. This is an initiative aimed at training regional civil servants on Open Data. So far, such trainings have been carried out for such employees of Chernivtsi, Lviv, Zakarpattia, Vinnytsia, and Rivne regions. By the end of 2025, it is planned to cover all regions of Ukraine. https://academy.data.gov.ua/. 
Also, in order to increase the level of professional knowledge and competencies of civil servants and officials of local self-government in the field of ensuring rights to access to public information, proper organization of the process of access to Open Data, a general short-term training program for civil servants was developed in co-operation with National Agency of Ukraine for Civil Service Affairs: https://pdp.nacs.gov.ua/courses/dostup-do-publichnoi-informatsii-dlia-derzhavnykh-sluzhbovtsiv-ta-posadovykh-osib-mistsevoho-samovriaduvannia. In 2023, 497 employees completed this training program, in 2024, by the end of June, according to the plan, more than 330 employees will complete this program.
On November 28, 2023, Ukraine launched the CDTO Campus project to accelerate digital transformation across the country. Ukraine is one of the first countries in the world to introduce the position of Chief Digital Transformation Officer - CDTO both in ministries and at the regional level. Within this new strategic project, civil servants working in the field of digital transformation will be trained, and the state will be provided with specialists qualified to lead and implement digital reforms. Within this project, digital leaders are taught the basics of forming and implementing an Open Data policy. https://www.cdto-campus.com/ua/cdto-campus-ua, https://www.cdto-campus.com/ua/programs-ua/obsie-formuvannya-ta-realizaciya-politiki-vidkritih-danih-cdto-campus-copy.

* If yes, please (1) provide the URL to an example and (2) briefly describe the approach used to ensure this transparency.
column4: Acording to "open-by-default" principle, all public information should be made available as Open Data
column7:
The publication of open datasets is carried out, in particular, according to the "Open-by-Default" principle, which consists in ensuring that information providers publish all public information as Open Data that is in their possession, except for information that is classified by law as information with limited access, and as well as information that is not subject to publication in accordance with the Law of Ukraine "On Access to Public Information".
It also means that providers shall proactively open new datasets, given the presumption of openness of public information. At the same time, the transformation (in particular, downloading from databases and, if necessary, depersonalization) of public information into Open Data is mandatory.
The Ministry informed data providers about this on the Unified State Web Portal of Open Data: https://diia.data.gov.ua/news/vazlivo-do-uvagi-koristuvaciv-jedinogo-derzavnogo-veb-portalu-vidkritix-danix  
This information is available for all visitors of the Portal, both data providers and data users.
